question: On the published optimization openings, how often does the original network strongly prefer the worse of two moves that two depths of search rank in the same order?
population: Select up to four positions per each of the original 48 optimization opening families. Within each family use ascending SHA-256 of the ASCII string 'sibling-diagnostic-v1|' plus the position ID, restricted to nonterminal boards with at least two legal moves. Freeze the resulting IDs before searches. The 15 prior held-out families get no searches in this diagnostic.
search: For the same original network run a fresh-state MultiPV=2 depth-9 and depth-13 search at each root. Retain both exact final principal lines, root-perspective scores and legal continuations, together with omissions, bounds, mates, changed ranks and other exclusions.
stable: Both searches must report the same legal ordered top two moves and unbounded integer centipawn scores on the final depth. A clear pair must have a margin of at least 20 centipawns at both depths, margins within 20 of each other, and both depth-13 scores within [-250,250].
measure: Measure the original static score of both actually constructed child positions. Convert each side-to-move child score into the root player's perspective before subtracting rank two from rank one. A gross inversion is a clear pair with static margin at most -12 centipawns. Account for unavailable child evaluations and report all measured dispositions, per family and per physical head.
outcome: This one diagnostic describes static move-ranking errors on exploratory openings. It makes no model edit or playing-strength estimate.
